plain_english_policy: This bill (HB414) would impose a hard cap on political action committee (PAC) contributions to Alabama candidates during any single election cycle—specifically **$1,000 per candidate**, regardless of whether the contribution is cash or in-kind. The legislation does not address individual donor limits, only PACs’ aggregate giving to a single candidate.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The bill signals a **pro-transparency/pro-regulation** stance on campaign finance by explicitly restricting corporate/interest-group influence via PACs. It would reduce the ability of well-funded PACs (often tied to corporations, unions, or advocacy groups) to dominate candidate financing in Alabama elections. The $1,000 limit is modest compared to federal standards but represents a **first state-level restriction** on PAC contributions in Alabama’s history (per the bill’s synopsis).
sponsorship_supports_position: The bill’s text and metadata suggest sponsors sought to curb PAC influence without targeting individual donors or party committees. No ideological inference beyond the bill’s explicit language is warranted.
evidence_quotes: Under existing law, there are no restrictions regarding the amount of contributions a political action committee may make to a political candidate.
This bill would limit contributions by a political action committee to a candidate to $1,000 per election.
review_reason: The bill’s intent is unambiguous: it creates a new legal cap on PAC contributions. No ceremonial or appropriations-only elements are present.
